United Kingdom (faction key `gbr`) — SURFACE FLEET ONLY, all six eras. Submarines (gbr_e50_sub … sub_b) and the SSBNs (gbr_e60_ssbn, ssbn_b) were excluded as owned by the other two workflows.

MEASURED under jsc (bundle = stub `var window=this;` + js/util.js js/config.js js/facts.js js/rules.js js/eras.js js/heavyair.js js/generations.js). 26 `gbr` hulls with layer:"sea" exist; 21 of them are warships proper (5 carriers, 2 cruisers, 5 destroyers, 5 frigates/"corvettes", 5 patrol) and they are defined in two places: eras.js lines 10173-10211 (e50-e00, one Object.assign block headed "ROYAL NAVY - era units") and rules.js lines 3054-3090 (e20).

THE HEADLINE. Britain's air-defence line — Sea Slug, Sea Dart, Sea Wolf, Sea Viper/Aster — is the thing the brief asked about, and the game has ONE of the four. Measured: of the 26 British sea hulls, 12 can engage an aircraft at all, and of those 12, ten are engaging with a dual-purpose GUN or a carrier air-wing abstraction. Exactly two hulls carry a real ship SAM, both of them in e20 (destroyer_b with Aster 30 + Aster 15, corvette_b with CAMM). Every era hull from 1962 to 2009 — County, Tiger, Type 42 Batch 1, Type 42 Batch 3, Invincible, Type 45 — has NO surface-to-air missile. The Type 45 Daring of e00 (gbr_e00_destroyer), the ship the brief singles out, resolves to a single American "Mk 45 Mod 4 127mm" with tgt {ground:1,air:0,sea:1,sub:0}. In the e00 era the best air-defence ship in Europe cannot shoot at an aeroplane.

THE SECOND HEADLINE. Thirteen of the 21 warships resolve to an AMERICAN weapon name. This is the IFV defect verbatim, transplanted to the sea. Measured names on British hulls: "Three 127mm/54 Mk 42 single mounts" (Daring 1952), "Nine 203mm/55 Mk 16 rapid-fire guns" (Swiftsure — the Des Moines 8in autoloader, on a ship whose own desc says triple 6in), "Terrier and Talos SAM launchers" (HMS Tiger, missiles the Royal Navy never owned, and with air:0 so it is not even a SAM), "Mk 13 launcher for SM-1MR and Harpoon" (HMS Broadsword — the Oliver Hazard Perry's launcher), "Two 127mm/54 Mk 45" (Type 42 Sheffield), "One 57mm Mk 110" (Type 23 with Sonar 2087 — the American LCS gun), and worst of all "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomahawk" on HMS Manchester, a Type 42 Batch 3.

LAND ATTACK — and here the game is RIGHT, which matters. No British surface warship has ever fired a land-attack cruise missile. RN Tomahawk is submarine-only: first British TLAM shot was HMS Splendid in 1998, from a torpedo tube, and it has stayed that way through Trafalgar and Astute. Neither destroyer_b nor gbr_e00_destroyer nor either Type 23 carries a land-attack round, and the eras.js block comment says so explicitly ("`ssgn`, because British land-attack missiles are fired from the torpedo tubes of an attack boat"). That is sound and should be left alone. The British contribution to the fight ashore is naval gunfire, and the game supports it: every British naval gun row measured carries ground:1, so a 4.5in can shell a beach — which is the real history (roughly 8,000 rounds of 4.5in fired in support of the land battle in the Falklands, HMS Glamorgan, Arrow, Alacrity, Avenger and the Type 42s taking turns on the gun line). The one place the prose breaks the rule is that Type 42 Batch 3 weapon NAME, which advertises Tomahawk on a British surface ship. That is precisely the Los Angeles defect: a name promising a capability the navy never had.

THE FALKLANDS TEST. Take the 1982 task group as the game models it. HMS Invincible fights with a Phalanx and nothing else — she went to war with a twin Sea Dart launcher and 22 rounds forward and no Phalanx at all (that came in the 1982-83 refit). HMS Sheffield fights with two American 5in guns and has no Sea Dart, on a class whose entire reason for existing is Sea Dart and whose own description in the file says "Sea Dart also shot down more aircraft than anything else in the British inventory that year". HMS Broadsword fights with a Perry's Mk 13 launcher and has no Sea Wolf and no Exocet, on a class whose description says "two Sea Wolf launchers, four Exocet and two Lynx". Not one ship in the 1982 order of battle is armed with what it was armed with.

WHAT IS SOUND. The roster SHAPE is right and was clearly thought about: no missileboat row in any era (the Royal Navy never operated a missile-armed fast attack craft, and the Brave boats were torpedo boats gone by 1970); no cruiser from e80 (HMS Blake paid off in 1979 and nothing replaced her); no fixed-wing AEW deck. Every service date checks out against real commissioning — Daring 1952, Whitby 1956, Tiger 1959, Brave Borderer 1960, Devonshire 1962, Leander 1963, Ark Royal post-Phantom-refit 1970, Sheffield 1975, Jersey 1976-77, Broadsword 1979, Invincible 1980, Leeds Castle 1981, Manchester 1982, Norfolk 1990, Sea Harrier FA2 1993, Tyne 2003, Sonar 2087 2006, Daring 2009, Queen Elizabeth 2017. I found NO anachronistic hull. Every anachronism in this fleet is in the weapon, not the date. The sonar figures are the British specialisation stated in numbers and they are the best in the game (corvette_b 11.0 and gbr_e00_corvette 10.6 are ranks 1 and 2 among all surface ships of all eight navies). The NAVGUN loop in generations.js has a deliberate `gbr` row that turns `navgun_76` into the 4.5in Mk 8 so a British escort never fires an OTO Melara; it currently fires on only three hulls and my edits put it to work on five more. And the e20 pair is genuinely excellent: corvette_b has gun + CAMM + Sting Ray and NO anti-ship missile, which is exactly right after Harpoon was withdrawn in 2023, and destroyer_b has Aster 30 + Aster 15 and no torpedo, which is exactly right because a Type 45 has no torpedo tubes fitted.

findings.whatTheGameHas: One weapon, w_e00_nato_destroyer, resolving to "Mk 45 Mod 4 127mm" with tgt {ground:1,air:0,sea:1,sub:0}. No Aster of any kind. Measured: the ship cannot engage an aircraft at all. The desc on the same row says "SAMPSON at the masthead and Aster beneath it give an air-defence capability at the top of the world".
findings.whatIsReal: HMS Daring commissioned 23 July 2009 with PAAMS/Sea Viper: SAMPSON multifunction array at 27 m, S1850M long-range radar, and a 48-cell Sylver A50 farm holding Aster 15 (30 km) and Aster 30 (120 km). First Aster 30 firing 2010, first multi-target salvo 2011. The gun is a 4.5in Mk 8 Mod 1, not an American Mk 45.
findings.fix: Replace the loadout with navgun_76 + sam_aster30 + sam_aster15 — exactly what the e20 destroyer_b already carries, because it is exactly the same ship. navgun_76 becomes the 4.5in Mk 8 automatically through the gbr row of the NAVGUN loop in generations.js.

findings.whatTheGameHas: w_e90_nato_destroyer, resolving to a weapon literally named "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomaha[wk]", warhead "he", proj "shell", tgt {ground:1,air:0,sea:1,sub:0}. An Arleigh Burke's magazine on a British Type 42; it names SM-2 and cannot shoot at aircraft, and it names Tomahawk on a surface ship of a navy that has never fired one.
findings.whatIsReal: HMS Manchester commissioned 16 December 1982. Type 42 Batch 3: one 4.5in Mk 8, twin-arm Sea Dart GWS.30 launcher, two Phalanx, two triple STWS tubes. No vertical launch system of any kind, ever; no Standard missile; and no surface-launched Tomahawk in Royal Navy service in any year — British TLAM is submarine-only, first fired by HMS Splendid in 1998 from a torpedo tube. Sea Dart served until HMS Edinburgh paid off on 6 June 2013.
findings.fix: Replace with navgun_76 + sam_seadart + ciws_phalanx. This is the same class of defect as the Los Angeles carrying only a torpedo while its prose boasts of Tomahawk tubes, running the other way: prose-grade capability asserted in a weapon name that the navy never possessed.

findings.whatTheGameHas: w_e80_nato_destroyer -> "Two 127mm/54 Mk 45", tgt {ground:1,air:0,sea:1,sub:0}. No Sea Dart. The desc on the same row opens "Sea Dart on a hull cut short to a price" and closes "Sea Dart also shot down more aircraft than anything else in the British inventory that year, which is the whole argument about this class in one sentence".
findings.whatIsReal: HMS Sheffield commissioned 16 February 1975. One 4.5in Mk 8 forward, twin Sea Dart GWS.30 launcher with 22 rounds, no CIWS as built. Sea Dart is a semi-active ramjet missile good to 40+ nmi and is credited with the largest share of the British missile kills of 1982.
findings.fix: Replace with navgun_76 + sam_seadart. Keep the class's known weakness in the missile's own stats (acc 0.80, not higher) rather than in its absence: Sea Dart worked against a high or medium target and was poor close inshore, which is how Coventry was lost on 25 May 1982.

findings.whatTheGameHas: w_e80_nato_corvette -> "Mk 13 launcher for SM-1MR and Harpoon", tgt {ground:1,air:1,sea:1,sub:0}. That is the single-arm launcher of the Oliver Hazard Perry class. The desc on the same row says "The first Royal Navy escort designed with no medium gun at all - two Sea Wolf launchers, four Exocet and two Lynx, and an anti-submarine suite that was the best in NATO outside the American fleet." The loadout contains none of those four things and does contain a gun.
findings.whatIsReal: HMS Broadsword commissioned 3 May 1979. Two six-round Sea Wolf GWS.25 launchers, four MM38 Exocet in single canisters forward, two Lynx HAS.2, two triple STWS-1 tubes (Mk 46, then Sting Ray from 1983), Type 2016 sonar, and no medium gun whatever. She never carried a Standard missile or a Harpoon.
findings.fix: Replace with sam_seawolf + ssm_exocet38 + asw_stingray, and give her NO gun. The missing gun is the point of the class and the absence should be visible in the loadout, not papered over with an American mount.

findings.whatTheGameHas: w_e60_nato_cruiser -> a weapon named "Terrier and Talos SAM launchers" with warhead "he", proj "shell" and tgt {ground:1,air:0,sea:1,sub:0}. Two American surface-to-air missiles, on a British cruiser that never carried either, in a row that is mechanically a gun and cannot engage an aircraft.
findings.whatIsReal: HMS Tiger commissioned 18 March 1959. Two twin 6in QF Mk N5 fully automatic mountings and three twin 3in/70 Mk 6 — the finest gun mountings the Royal Navy ever installed and so unreliable that Tiger and Blake were rebuilt as helicopter cruisers between 1965 and 1972 instead. The Royal Navy never operated Terrier or Talos in any ship in any year.
findings.fix: Replace with a new literal row w_e60_gbr_cruiser: "Two twin 6in QF Mk N5 and three twin 3in/70", air:1 (the 3in/70 was a dual-purpose mount) and a low acc of 0.50 to carry the unreliability that actually ended the class.

findings.whatTheGameHas: w_e50_nato_cruiser -> "Nine 203mm/55 Mk 16 rapid-fire guns in thr[ee triples]". That is the Des Moines-class autoloading 8in — the heaviest cruiser gun the United States ever built. The desc two fields away says "Triple 6in turrets and enough armour to matter".
findings.whatIsReal: HMS Swiftsure commissioned 22 June 1944. Nine 6in (152 mm) BL Mk XXIII in three triple turrets, hand-worked, plus ten 4in QF Mk XVI. Britain never built an 8in gun cruiser after the County class of 1928 and none was in service in the 1950s.
findings.fix: Replace with a new literal row w_e50_gbr_cruiser: "Nine 6in BL Mk XXIII in three triples", tgt air:0 — the Mk XXIII was a surface mounting with no anti-air role, which is a real and interesting difference from the Tiger that follows it.

findings.whatTheGameHas: w_e60_nato_destroyer -> "Two 127mm/54 Mk 42", tgt {ground:1,air:0,sea:1,sub:0}. A unit whose full name is "County-class guided missile destroyer" carries no missile of any kind and cannot engage an aircraft. The desc says "Six thousand tonnes to carry one Sea Slug launcher".
findings.whatIsReal: HMS Devonshire commissioned 15 November 1962. Two twin 4.5in QF Mk 6, one twin Sea Slug GWS.1 launcher aft with a magazine running most of the hull, two quad Sea Cat, one Wessex helicopter. Sea Slug is a beam rider: the ship must hold a radar beam on the target and the missile crawls up it, which works against a high bomber and not against anything low or crossing.
findings.fix: Replace with w_e60_gbr_destroyer ("Two twin 4.5in QF Mk 6") + sam_seaslug, where sam_seaslug is authored with acc 0.58, reload 11.0 and intercept 1.05 so that its limitations are in its statistics. Do NOT add Sea Cat: GWS.20-24 was on almost every British hull from 1962 and has no undisputed Falklands kill; a system that did not work is better modelled as no weapon than as a weak one.

findings.whatTheGameHas: w_e00_nato_corvette -> "One 57mm Mk 110", tgt {ground:1,air:1,sea:1,sub:0}. The Mk 110 is the Bofors 57 mm of the American Littoral Combat Ship and the Legend-class cutter; no British warship has ever mounted one. And the hull carries sonar 10.6, the second-highest surface figure in the entire game, with NO weapon that can attack a submarine — the desc calls it "the single best anti-submarine sensor in this game".
findings.whatIsReal: Sonar 2087 entered service on HMS Westminster in 2006 and was fitted to eight of the sixteen Type 23s. Their fit in that decade: one 4.5in Mk 8, 32-cell Sea Wolf GWS.26 VLS, eight Harpoon Block 1C (fitted from 1994), two twin Magazine Torpedo Launch System tubes firing Sting Ray, and a Merlin or Lynx.
findings.fix: Replace with navgun_76 + sam_seawolf + ssm_harpoon + asw_stingray. Note that ship-launched ASW is thin across this whole game — measured, only 2 of 26 British sea hulls and a small minority of all era hulls anywhere can attack a submarine — but it costs Britain more than anyone, because ASW is the one thing this navy is stated to be best at.

findings.whatTheGameHas: Measured: not one British hull in any era carries an anti-ship missile. The only ship-killing weapons in the fleet are guns and one 1958 torpedo boat.
findings.whatIsReal: From 1973 to 2023 a Royal Navy escort essentially always had one. MM38 Exocet went into the County class from 1973, the Type 21 Amazons, the Type 22 Batch 1s and the Exocet-converted Leanders. Harpoon Block 1C replaced it on the Type 22 Batch 3 and the Type 23 from the early 1990s and was withdrawn in 2023 with no replacement. The gap in the real timeline is at both ends — before 1973 and after 2023 — and the game has flattened it into one continuous absence.
findings.fix: ssm_exocet38 (a new MM38 row, 42 km and anti-ship only, distinct from the existing ssm_exocet which is the 180 km MM40 Block 3) on the Type 22; ssm_harpoon on both Type 23s. Leave the e20 corvette_b with nothing, because 2023 is when Harpoon went, and its desc already says exactly that.

findings.whatTheGameHas: "Air wing of ~90 aircraft" on the Audacious class and on the 1970 Ark Royal, and "Air wing of 75+ aircraft" on Queen Elizabeth. These are the shared American carrier rows.
findings.whatIsReal: HMS Eagle's air group ran around 60 machines at its largest. The 1970 post-refit Ark Royal embarked roughly 39: 12 Phantom FG.1, 14 Buccaneer S.2, 4 Gannet AEW.3, a Gannet COD, 6 Sea King and 2 Wessex. Queen Elizabeth's design load is 24 F-35B plus about 14 helicopters; Op Fortis in 2021 sailed with 18 F-35B, eight of them American. Separately the Audacious class carried sixteen 4.5in QF Mk VI in eight twin turrets, a substantial gun battery the game does not represent at all.
findings.fix: Not proposed as an edit here. The carrier weapon rows are a shared abstraction used by every faction, and changing them reaches well outside the British fleet. Recorded so the owner knows the numbers are American.

findings.whatTheGameHas: All five carry the shared `hmg`, "12.7mm HMG". Each desc names a different and larger gun: the Island class "a 40 mm on the bow", the River Batch 1 "A 20 mm gun", the River Batch 2 "a 30 mm gun and a flight deck".
findings.whatIsReal: Ford class: one 40 mm Bofors and one 20 mm Oerlikon. Island and Castle: one 40 mm/60 Mk 9. River Batch 1: one 20 mm Oerlikon. River Batch 2: one 30 mm DS30M Mk 2.
findings.fix: Not proposed. `hmg` is the game-wide patrol-boat abstraction and every navy's small craft use it; changing it for Britain alone would create an inconsistency rather than remove one. Worth a single desc softening if the owner cares, not a loadout change.

findings.whatTheGameHas: The shared `torpedo` row, "heavyweight torpedo", dmg 340, range 9.0, tgt {ground:0,air:0,sea:1,sub:1}. The hull has sonar 0.
findings.whatIsReal: Brave Borderer and Brave Swordsman, launched 1958, carried two 21in tubes firing the wartime Mk VIII* — an anti-ship torpedo, straight-running, with no anti-submarine capability. dmg 340 is the same figure the game gives a DM2A4 Seehecht. And a boat with no sonar cannot find a submarine to shoot at in the first place, so sub:1 is inert as well as wrong.
findings.fix: Not proposed as an edit — `torpedo` is shared with fra_e60_patrol, deu_e50_patrol and deu_e60_patrol, so a private clone would be needed and the gain is small. Recorded.

findings.whatTheGameHas: navgun_76 + sam_aster30 + sam_aster15, no anti-ship missile. The desc says "It was built with no anti-ship missile whatsoever and had none for fourteen years, until NSM began appearing in 2023-24".
findings.whatIsReal: The Naval Strike Missile interim fit went first to the Type 23s (HMS Somerset and HMS Sutherland in 2023-24) and is being spread across a handful of Type 45s. A small minority of hulls carry it.
findings.fix: Not proposed. The desc already hedges with "began appearing", and giving every Type 45 an NSM would overstate a fit that only a few ships have. Recorded as a prose/loadout tension that is currently on the right side of the line.

findings.unit: js/eras.js, the ROYAL NAVY era-units block header
findings.whatTheGameHas: The header asserts that every British hull must point at a `w_e**_nato_<role>` id because "those ids are 784 LITERAL rows at the head of this file, not generated, so a British corvette invented with a `w_e50_gbr_corvette` would dereference undefined on its first target evaluation and throw".
findings.whatIsReal: Measured: 66 distinct `w_e**_gbr_*` literal weapon rows already exist in the same file — w_e50_gbr_rifle, w_e50_gbr_mbt, w_e00_gbr_sead and so on. The namespace is in daily use for the British land and air forces. The real constraint is only that a new id must be WRITTEN, not that it cannot exist. As it stands the comment reads as a justification for a defect rather than a description of one.
findings.fix: Correct the paragraph to say what is actually true: the naval rows point at the American ids because nobody has yet authored British ones, and where the ordnance is the identity a British row should be written — which is exactly what the file already does for the 4.5in Mk 8, Sting Ray, Spearfish and Trident.

findings.unit: the entire British surface fleet, all six eras
findings.whatTheGameHas: No land-attack missile on any British surface warship in any era. destroyer_b and gbr_e00_destroyer have none; both Type 23s have none; the eras.js block comment states the reason under `ssgn`.
findings.whatIsReal: Correct, and it is one of the sharpest facts about this navy. The Royal Navy has never fired a surface-launched land-attack cruise missile. Tomahawk is carried and fired only by the attack submarines — HMS Splendid fired the first British TLAM in 1998, and the capability passed from Trafalgar to Astute through the torpedo tubes. This is the right answer under realism-over-symmetry: Britain simply does not have what an Arleigh Burke has, and the roster should keep saying so.
findings.fix: None. Do not add a land-attack round to any British surface hull. The only correction needed is removing the false Tomahawk claim from the Type 42 Batch 3 weapon NAME, which is listed as a separate fatal finding above.

findings.whatTheGameHas: Measured: every British naval gun row carries tgt ground:1, so a 4.5in can shell a target ashore.
findings.whatIsReal: Correct, and it is the British land-attack contribution. Roughly eight thousand 4.5in rounds were fired in support of the land battle in the Falklands, from Glamorgan, Arrow, Alacrity, Avenger, Ambuscade, Antrim and the Type 42s working a nightly gun line. Naval gunfire IS land attack and the game already knows it.
findings.fix: None. Preserved through my edits: every replacement British gun row keeps ground:1. The one deliberate loss is the Type 22 Batch 1, which drops to ground:0 because it genuinely had no medium gun and genuinely could not take a turn on the gun line.

findings.whatTheGameHas: No `missileboat` row for gbr in any era, and no `cruiser` row from e80.
findings.whatIsReal: Both correct and both explained in the file. The Royal Navy has never operated a missile-armed fast attack craft; its last fast boats were the two Brave-class torpedo boats, gone by 1970, and after that the small end of the fleet is constabulary work — which the Ford, Island, Castle and River descs all say in their own words. HMS Blake, the last cruiser, paid off in 1979 and nothing replaced her; an Invincible is a carrier whatever the Treasury called it and a Type 45 is a destroyer.
findings.fix: None. This is realism-over-symmetry working exactly as intended and should not be 'filled in'.

findings.whatTheGameHas: A `service` field on every era hull.
findings.whatIsReal: Checked one by one against real commissioning: Daring 1952, Eagle 1951 (Audacious class), Ford class 1954, Whitby 1956, Tiger 1959, Brave Borderer 1960, Devonshire 1962, Leander 1963, Ark Royal post-Phantom-refit 1970, Sheffield 1975, Jersey 1976-77 (Island class), Broadsword 1979, Invincible 1980, Leeds Castle 1981, Manchester 1982, Norfolk 1990, Sea Harrier FA2 1993, Tyne 2003, Sonar 2087 2006, Daring 2009, Queen Elizabeth 2017. Not one is wrong, and the from:/to: windows sit correctly against them.
findings.fix: None. Worth stating plainly because the brief warned that an earlier audit missed units with no service field: I checked the ones without it too — the five e20 hulls in rules.js carry from:"e20" and no service string, and all five are present-day ships in current commission, so there is nothing to catch.

findings.whatTheGameHas: sonar 11.0 and 10.6 — measured as ranks 1 and 2 among all surface ships of all eight navies, ahead of the American destroyer_n at 9.5.
findings.whatIsReal: Correct and deliberate. Sonar 2087 is a low-frequency active and passive towed array with no equal in another European fleet, fitted to eight of sixteen Type 23s from 2006, and paired with a Merlin HM2 it is the best anti-submarine system in this game. generations.js also gives gbr a naval domain multiplier of 1.00 — level with the United States and above France at 0.90 and Germany at 0.72 — with a comment naming the Type 23 and the Astute as the reason.
findings.fix: None to the sensor. But the sensor deserves a weapon behind it — see the gbr_e00_corvette and gbr_e90_corvette findings — because a hull that detects better than anyone and cannot shoot is a specialisation the player never gets to use.

findings.whatTheGameHas: All three resolve to "4.5in Mk 8 (114mm)", dmg 62, range 9.2, acc 0.82, tgt {ground:1,air:1,sea:1,sub:0} — not an OTO Melara, even though two of them are authored carrying navgun_76.
findings.whatIsReal: Correct, and it is the NAVGUN loop at the tail of generations.js doing its job: a gbr row substitutes the 4.5 inch Mk 8 into any British weapon whose name matches /OTO 76mm/. Britain never bought the Italian gun for its escorts — the Mk 8 is heavier and slower-firing and built for naval gunfire support, which is exactly the comment already in the file. The Mk 8 entered service on HMS Bristol in 1971, so it is right for everything from the Type 42 onward and wrong for anything before it, which is why my edits author separate e50 and e60 rows rather than extending this loop backwards.
findings.fix: None. My edits deliberately route five more British hulls (both Type 42s, both e00/e90 Type 23s, the Type 45) through navgun_76 so the NAVGUN gbr row covers eight hulls instead of three.

findings.whatTheGameHas: No anti-submarine weapon. Measured: destroyer_b cannot attack a submarine.
findings.whatIsReal: Correct. The Type 45 has no torpedo tubes fitted — the Magazine Torpedo Launch System was designed in and left out. Its anti-submarine capability is the embarked Merlin or Wildcat, not the ship. An audit that 'fixed' this by handing the Daring a Sting Ray would be inventing a capability to balance a roster.
findings.fix: None. Leave it exactly as it is.

edits.why: Author the British ship-SAM line, the 1970s Exocet and the Limbo mortar. All five sit in the existing "European naval ordnance" block, which is the place this file already reserves for ordnance that IS the national identity (the 4.5in Mk 8, Spearfish, Sting Ray). Sea Slug, Sea Dart, Sea Wolf and Aster are four different weapons that replaced one another for reasons, and a single shared row would erase the whole argument. Sea Cat is deliberately not authored: it was on almost every British hull from 1962 and has no undisputed Falklands kill, and a system that did not work is better modelled as no weapon than as a weak one. MM38 gets its own row because the existing ssm_exocet is the MM40 Block 3 at 180 km, four times the 42 km round the 1970s ships carried, and it is anti-ship only where MM40 has a land-attack mode.

edits.why: gbr_e50_corvette, HMS Whitby, commissioned 10 July 1956. The unit's own full name calls it a first-rate ANTI-SUBMARINE frigate and it could not attack a submarine; its gun was the American twin 3in/50 Mk 33, which no Royal Navy escort ever mounted. Real fit: one twin 4.5in QF Mk 6 forward, one twin 40 mm Bofors STAAG aft, and two Limbo Mk 10 mortars - the ASW armament being the entire reason the class exists.

edits.why: gbr_e50_destroyer, HMS Daring, commissioned 8 March 1952. Two faults in one field: the desc on this very row says "three twin 4.5in Mk 6 turrets" while the loadout said "Three 127mm/54 Mk 42 single mounts", and the Mk 42 did not enter American service until 1955, three years after this hull's own service date. Left gun-only on purpose: the Daring was built as a gun destroyer and I will not assert an ASW mortar fit I cannot pin down ship by ship.

gbr_e50_cruiser, HMS Swiftsure, commissioned 22 June 1944. Carried the Des Moines-class nine-gun 8in autoloader, the heaviest cruiser battery the United States ever built, while its own desc says "Triple 6in turrets". Britain laid down no 8in cruiser after 1928 and had none in service. Real fit: nine 6in BL Mk XXIII in three hand-worked triples, with no anti-air role - hence air:0, which is the honest difference between this ship and the Tiger that follows it.

edits.why: gbr_e60_corvette, HMS Leander, commissioned 27 March 1963. Carried an American single 5in/54 Mk 42 while its own desc says "A twin 4.5in forward", and had no anti-submarine weapon on a hull with sonar 5.0. Real fit: one twin 4.5in QF Mk 6 forward, one Limbo Mk 10 aft, a Wasp HAS.1 with a homing torpedo.

gbr_e60_destroyer, HMS Devonshire, commissioned 15 November 1962. A unit whose full name is "County-class guided missile destroyer" had no missile and could not engage an aircraft. Sea Slug is the ship - six thousand tonnes built round one twin launcher and a magazine running most of the hull - and its limitations belong in its statistics rather than in its absence, which is why sam_seaslug carries acc 0.58, reload 11.0 and intercept 1.05. No Sea Cat and no Limbo added: Sea Cat has no undisputed Falklands kill, and I could not verify a Limbo fit on this class - the County's anti-submarine weapon was its Wessex.

gbr_e60_cruiser, HMS Tiger, commissioned 18 March 1959. Carried a weapon named "Terrier and Talos SAM launchers" - two American missiles the Royal Navy never operated in any ship in any year - implemented as a gun with tgt air:0, so it was not even a SAM. Real fit: two twin 6in QF Mk N5 and three twin 3in/70 Mk 6, automatic, dual-purpose, and famously unreliable.

edits.why: gbr_e80_corvette, HMS Broadsword, commissioned 3 May 1979. Carried the Oliver Hazard Perry's Mk 13 launcher with SM-1 and Harpoon while its own desc says "The first Royal Navy escort designed with no medium gun at all - two Sea Wolf launchers, four Exocet and two Lynx". The new loadout has NO GUN, deliberately: the missing 4.5in is the defining fact about the class, it is why the Type 21s and Type 42s took the Falklands gun line instead, and the absence should be visible rather than papered over with an American mount. Sting Ray rather than a Mk 46 because the torpedo entered British service in 1983, inside this era window.

gbr_e80_destroyer, HMS Sheffield, commissioned 16 February 1975. Carried two American 5in/54 Mk 45 and no Sea Dart, on the class whose own desc ends "Sea Dart also shot down more aircraft than anything else in the British inventory that year, which is the whole argument about this class in one sentence". Real fit: one 4.5in Mk 8, twin Sea Dart GWS.30 with 22 rounds, and no close-in weapon system - which the desc also says and which the loadout should now reflect by having no CIWS while the Batch 3 below does.

gbr_e80_carrier, HMS Invincible, commissioned 11 July 1980. The game gave her the Phalanx she did not have in 1980-82 and withheld the Sea Dart she did have. She commissioned with a twin-arm GWS.30 launcher and 22 rounds on the forecastle; Phalanx arrived in the 1982-83 post-Falklands refit, part-way through this era window, so both belong on an e80 hull. Sea Dart came out in the 1999 refit to lengthen the flight deck.

gbr_e90_corvette, HMS Norfolk, commissioned 1 June 1990. The gun is already right - NAVGUN turns w_e90_nato_corvette into the 4.5in Mk 8 - so it is kept and three systems are appended instead. The desc names "a 4.5in Mk 8, Sea Wolf, Harpoon and a Lynx" and three of the four were missing, and the hull carried sonar 8.4 with nothing to shoot at a submarine with. Real fit: 32-cell vertical Sea Wolf GWS.26, two quad Harpoon Block 1C from 1994, Sting Ray from the Magazine Torpedo Launch System.

gbr_e90_destroyer, HMS Manchester, commissioned 16 December 1982. The worst single line in this fleet: a weapon named "90-96 cell Mk 41 VLS with SM-2/ESSM/Tomahawk" on a British Type 42 - an Arleigh Burke's magazine, a missile the Royal Navy never bought, and a false claim of surface-launched land attack that Britain has never had in any ship in any year. Real fit: one 4.5in Mk 8, twin Sea Dart GWS.30, two Phalanx - which the desc itself says the Batch 3 was given and the earlier hulls went to war without. Sea Dart served until HMS Edinburgh paid off on 6 June 2013.

gbr_e90_carrier, HMS Illustrious with Sea Harrier FA2. The Phalanx it already has is correct for the 1990s; what is missing is the Sea Dart launcher, which the Invincible class kept until the refits of 1999-2000, i.e. for most of this era window. Appended rather than replaced so the close-in gun stays.

gbr_e00_corvette, the Type 23 with Sonar 2087, in service 2006. Carried "One 57mm Mk 110" - the Bofors gun of the American Littoral Combat Ship, which no British warship has ever mounted - and had the second-highest sonar figure of any surface ship in the game (10.6) with nothing that could attack a submarine. Real fit in that decade: 4.5in Mk 8, 32-cell Sea Wolf GWS.26, eight Harpoon Block 1C, Sting Ray from the MTLS tubes. This is the hull the whole British naval identity rests on and it should be able to use its sensor.

gbr_e00_destroyer, HMS Daring, commissioned 23 July 2009 - the finding the brief asked about directly. The best air-defence ship in Europe had tgt air:0 and could not engage an aircraft, while carrying an American Mk 45 it has never mounted.
